newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African shares seen positive, but consolidating.
newsitem.headline: S.African shares seen positive, but consolidating.

text.p: South African shares are set to continue their upward drive next week, but momentum is slowing and advances will be modest, dealers and portfolio managers said on Friday.
The last two weeks have seen the all-share index climb to new all-time highs, but recently the performance has been more mixed as negative factors have crept in to the market.
U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan warned on Wednesday that U.S. stock prices may have risen too far and hinted that the Federal Reserve could hike U.S. interest rates.

The comments did not -- as some feared -- produce a meltdown, but they kept a firm grip on positive sentiment in South Africa's industrials market which is wary of signs that Wall Street's bull run may collapse.

Some recent economic data has also been subdued. Figures released on Thursday showed annual private sector credit growth was 17.07 percent in January against a revised 16.09 percent in December. A Reuters consensus poll of economist had forecast private credit as expanding 15.3 percent against 15.75 percent.
January money supply came in at 16.89 percent -- also above market expectations of a 15.8 percent rise.
Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals told Reuters the worse-than-expected figures showed little scope for an easing of the country's tight monetary policy in the near future.
"One should not over-react to this, and see what happens in February. But it certainly confirms that there is no room at this stage for relaxing on the monetary policy," he said
Stock watchers said these factors would temper sentiment next week, but not seriously reverse it.
"The market has had a good start to the year, but from here on I think it will be a little more pedestrian," said Chris Logan, portfolio manager at BOE Asset Management.
Underlying fundamentals are still firm. The rand, whose collapse was responsible for so much economic woe in 1996, is holding steady after dizzy gains at the start of the year.
Another source of goodwill is the bullion price which at last appears to have bumped off the bottom of its long collapse.
Spot gold has roared past the $360 an ounce level as buyers have poured back into the yellow metal on the back of a rally in platinum prices.

South African gold shares have also launched a strong recovery on the back of the bullion bounce and the upward trend is expected to continue. "The gold price was just deeply oversold. There should be some kicking back to a more realistic level," said one dealer.
After trade, GDP and inflation data were also posted this week there will be few local economic figures to guide South African markets before the budget on March 12.
But next week will see several heavyweight corporates release results.

On Tuesday diamond giant De Beers Ltd is expected to post a cut and polished set of year results and on the same day financial services firm RMB Holdings Ltd and investment group NSA Investments Ltd will post half-year results.
On Thursday mining house Anglovaal Ltd will publish its interim figures while appliance firm Daewoo Electronics South Africa Ltd will bring out year results.
While the figures may effect individual share prices, dealers said they are not expected to influence the whole market in any way.
